# dbt_marketing/models/staging/stg_touchpoints.sql (42 lines)
-- One row per marketing touch, cleaned and typed. No business logic.
--
-- Staging's job is to make the source safe to build on: stable column names,
-- explicit types, trimmed strings. Anything that involves a decision about
-- meaning (what counts as a session, which touch gets credit) belongs
-- downstream. Keeping that line sharp is what makes it possible to say
-- "the source is fine, the logic is wrong" when a number looks off.

with source as (

    select * from {{ source('raw', 'touchpoints') }}

),

renamed as (

    select
        -- Composite key. The generator has no touch-level id, so we build one
        -- from the natural key; the tests below assert it is actually unique.
        cast(user_id as varchar) || '-' || cast(touch_number as varchar)
            as touchpoint_id,

        cast(user_id as bigint)          as user_id,

        -- Left 0-based here on purpose: renaming is staging's job, re-indexing
        -- is not. int_touchpoints_sessionized derives a 1-based touch_seq.
        cast(touch_number as integer)    as touch_index,

        -- raw arrives as TIMESTAMP_NS from pandas. Nothing here needs
        -- nanoseconds, and the wider type propagates awkwardly into joins.
        cast(touched_at as timestamp)    as touched_at,

        lower(trim(channel))             as channel,
        lower(trim(campaign))            as campaign,

        cast(cost as double)             as touch_cost_usd

    from source

)

select * from renamed

# dbt_marketing/models/staging/_staging__models.yml (69 lines)
version: 2

models:
  - name: stg_touchpoints
    description: One row per marketing touch. Typed and renamed, no logic.
    columns:
      - name: touchpoint_id
        description: "{user_id}-{touch_index}. Synthetic, unique per touch."
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: user_id
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: touch_index
        description: 0-based position within the user's journey, as generated.
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: touched_at
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: channel
        data_tests:
          - not_null
          - accepted_values:
              # Locked to channels.py. A new channel must be added there
              # first, which is the point - the test fails loudly rather than
              # letting an unknown channel leak through into attribution.
              #
              # `arguments:` is required from dbt 1.11; passing `values:` at the
              # top level still works but emits a deprecation warning.
              arguments:
                values:
                  - display
                  - paid_social
                  - paid_search
                  - organic_search
                  - email
                  - direct
      - name: campaign
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: touch_cost_usd
        description: USD paid for this touch. Zero for organic and direct.
        data_tests: [not_null]

  - name: stg_conversions
    description: One row per user, converters and non-converters.
    columns:
      - name: user_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: has_converted
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: reported_touch_count
        description: Generator's touch count; reconciled against a recount downstream.
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: converted_at
        description: Null for non-converters - the only intentional null here.
      - name: revenue_usd
        data_tests: [not_null]

  - name: stg_kaggle_ads
    description: Real ad-level aggregates. Calibration benchmark only.
    columns:
      - name: ad_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: gender
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: ["M", "F"]
      - name: spend_usd
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: clicks
        data_tests: [not_null]
